# Product of intervals, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_mul_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An interval $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ that contains $x y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, with $X = [x_l, x_u]$ and $Y = [y_l, y_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $y_l = y_{l0} + y_{l1}$, $y_u = y_{u0} + y_{u1}$, $z_l = z_{l0} + z_{l1}$, $z_u = z_{u0} + z_{u1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $Y = [y_l, y_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $y_l = +\infty$ and $y_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $y_l \le y_u$, $y_l < +\infty$, $y_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when an operand is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $x y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For bounded $X$ and $Y$ and a bounded $Z$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, x y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $\ell - z_l \le A\,\lvert \ell\rvert + B$ and $z_u - h \le A\,\lvert h\rvert + B$, with the constants $A$ and $B$ below. A bound of $Z$ is the bound of the range exactly in no case claimed. For nonempty operands, an infinite bound of the range is returned as such.
- **I6.** For nonempty $X$ and $Y$: if an operand is $[0, 0]$, $Z$ is $[0, 0]$, the other operand unbounded included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the rule of interval arithmetic).
- **I5.** For bounded $X$ and $Y$, $Z$ is bounded when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max} - 2}$. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max} - 2}$ is $2^{1022}$ for `double`, $2^{126}$ for `float`.

The constants of the bound, from `gen/claims.json`: $A$ is `(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^6)*up(unit(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2)))+2*u^2)*(1+unit(mul_2_2))/(1-u)` and $B$ is `2*(1+u)^2*(1/2*up((1+u)^6)*eta+up((1+u)*(2*(1+u)^5*eta+tiny(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2))+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))+eta+(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^6)*up(unit(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2)))+2*u^2)/(1-u)*tiny(mul_2_2)`, where `up( )` is a constant as `T` rounds it up (the $E$, $G$, $H$ of a radius) and `unit( )`, `tiny( )` are the constants of the center's kernel; $N$ is the smallest normal number of `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| $A / u^2$ | $1.0000000000000013 \times 10^{1}$ | $1.0000006794931444 \times 10^{1}$ |
| $B / N$ | $2.0000000000000031 \times 10^{0}$ | $2.000001668930274 \times 10^{0}$ |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_mul_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalMul2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalMul2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_mul_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_mul_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the least and the greatest of the four products of bounds by mul_ext_2_2 (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_mul_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_mul_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_ext_2_2`](mul_ext_2_2.md), [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md).

```
# The product of two intervals with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Two
# limbs"), without a branch: the four products of bounds by mul_ext_2_2, the least of the four
# lower values and the greatest of the four upper ones by the comparison of 2-limb numbers, then
# the empty set as in interval_add_2. Tightness for bounded operands and a bounded result: each
# bound within A |v| + B of the bound v of the exact range, with the constants of mul_dir_2_2
# (v -> v - A |v| - B does not decrease, A being below 1, so the least of four values each close
# to its product is close to the least product); an infinite bound of the exact range is that
# bound of the result; a nonempty operand that is [0, 0] gives [0, 0] (zero_factor). Bounded when
# the exact range is within a quarter of the overflow threshold. The largest listing of the
# milestone: an ordinary inline function, not forced inline (milestone2.md, "Inlining and compile
# time" and question 13).

(a0, a1, e0, e1) = mul_ext_2_2(xl0, xl1, yl0, yl1)
(b0, b1, f0, f1) = mul_ext_2_2(xl0, xl1, yu0, yu1)
(c0, c1, g0, g1) = mul_ext_2_2(xu0, xu1, yl0, yl1)
(d0, d1, h0, h1) = mul_ext_2_2(xu0, xu1, yu0, yu1)
ma  = lt_2_2(b0, b1, a0, a1)
p0  = select(ma, b0, a0)
p1  = select(ma, b1, a1)
mb  = lt_2_2(d0, d1, c0, c1)
q0  = select(mb, d0, c0)
q1  = select(mb, d1, c1)
mc  = lt_2_2(q0, q1, p0, p1)
l0  = select(mc, q0, p0)
l1  = select(mc, q1, p1)
na  = lt_2_2(e0, e1, f0, f1)
r0  = select(na, f0, e0)
r1  = select(na, f1, e1)
nb  = lt_2_2(g0, g1, h0, h1)
s0  = select(nb, h0, g0)
s1  = select(nb, h1, g1)
nc  = lt_2_2(r0, r1, s0, s1)
u0  = select(nc, s0, r0)
u1  = select(nc, s1, r1)
nx  = lt(xl0, const inf)
ny  = lt(yl0, const inf)
ne  = and(nx, ny)
mi  = neg(const inf)
zl0 = select(ne, l0, const inf)
zl1 = select(ne, l1, 0)
zu0 = select(ne, u0, mi)
zu1 = select(ne, u1, 0)
```
